In this paper, we propose GANICE (GAN for Interventional Conditional Estimation) with several advantages: it (i) specifies the conditional interventional distribution for each treatment--covariate state as the causal estimation target; (ii) estimates the conditional distribution such that its averaged Wasserstein risk is minimized; (iii) attains minimax optimality. GANICE achieves these advantages through the extended Wasserstein distance and cell-normalized estimation, with minimax bounds based on Wasserstein GAN oracle inequalities and an anisotropic Assouad construction; Besov theory characterizes the cellwise critics. Our experiments show that GANICE outperforms existing methods on most benchmarks.
author: Shu Tamano, Masaaki Imaizumi

title: Minimax Rates and Spectral Distillation for Tree Ensembles
content:
arXiv:2605.11841v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Tree ensembles such as random forests (RFs) and gradient boosting machines (GBMs) are among the most widely used supervised learners, yet their theoretical properties remain incompletely understood. We adopt a spectral perspective on these algorithms, with two main contributions. First, we derive minimax-optimal convergence for RF regression, showing that, under mild regularity conditions on tree growth, the eigenvalue decay of the induced kernel operator governs the statistical rate. Second, we exploit this spectral viewpoint to develop compression schemes for tree ensembles. For RFs, leading eigenfunctions of the kernel operator capture the dominant predictive directions; for GBMs, leading singular vectors of the smoother matrix play an analogous role. Learning nonlinear maps for these spectral representations yields distilled models that are orders of magnitude smaller than the originals while maintaining competitive predictive performance. Our methods compare favorably to state of the art algorithms for forest pruning and rule extraction, with applications to resource constrained computing.
author: Binh Duc Vu, David S. Watson

title: Information-Theoretic Generalization Bounds for Sequential Decision Making
content:
arXiv:2605.12190v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Information-theoretic generalization bounds based on the supersample construction are a central tool for algorithm-dependent generalization analysis in the batch i.i.d. setting. However, existing supersample conditional mutual information (CMI) bounds do not directly apply to sequential decision-making problems such as online learning, streaming active learning, and bandits, where data are revealed adaptively and the learner evolves along a causal trajectory. To address this limitation, we develop a sequential supersample framework that separates the learner filtration from a proof-side enlargement used for ghost-coordinate comparisons. Under a row-wise exchangeability assumption, the sequential generalization gap is controlled by sequential CMI, a sum of roundwise selector--loss information terms. We also establish a Bernstein-type refinement that yields faster rates under suitable variance conditions. The resulting bounds specialize to online learning, streaming active learning with importance weighting, and stochastic multi-armed bandits.
author: Futoshi Futami, Masahiro Fujisawa

title: PPG2ECG: Physiology-Guided Latent Rectified Flow for Electro-Hemodynamic PPG-to-ECG Generation
content:
arXiv:2605.12541v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Electrocardiography (ECG) is the clinical standard for cardiac assessment but requires dedicated hardware that does not scale to daily-life monitoring. Photoplethysmography (PPG) is ubiquitous in wearables but lacks ECG-specific diagnostic morphology and is corrupted by motion and sensor noise. PPG-to-ECG generation aims to bridge this gap by recovering electrical morphology and timing from peripheral pulse signals. However, existing methods largely rely on statistical alignment and data-driven generation. They fail to explicitly structure the latent space around physiology-aware electro-hemodynamic factors and lack constraints from forward physiological dynamics. To address these challenges, we propose PPG2ECG, a physiology-guided latent rectified flow framework. PPG2ECG introduces an electro-hemodynamic simulator that co-models ECG and PPG through shared cardiac phase dynamics. Guided by this simulator, a Physiology-Aware AutoEncoder learns a structured electro-hemodynamic latent space. Then we integrate this simulator guidance into a PPG-conditioned latent rectified flow, enforcing ECG-side morphology consistency and ECG-to-PPG forward hemodynamic consistency during generative transport. Experiments on the large-scale MC-MED dataset demonstrate that PPG2ECG significantly improves PPG-to-ECG generation and downstream cardiovascular disease classification, proving its ability to generate ECGs that are both signal-faithful and physiologically plausible under the ECG-to-PPG hemodynamic pathway
author: Xiaoda Wang, Minxiao Wang, Kaiqiao Han, Defu Cao, Ching Chang, Yidan Shi, Runze Yan, Xiao Luo, Yan Liu, Xiao Hu, Yizhou Sun, Wei Wang, Carl Yang

title: CurveBench: A Benchmark for Exact Topological Reasoning over Nested Jordan Curves
content:
arXiv:2605.14068v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We introduce CurveBench, a benchmark for visual topological reasoning. Given an image of disjoint closed curves, a model must recover the tree of adjacent regions rooted at the exterior. The benchmark contains 756 hand-drawn images, ranging from simple configurations to maze-like and densely packed arrangements. Each image has a manually verified reference tree. We evaluate predictions by exact tree matching with the exterior root fixed. Gemini 3.1 Pro, the strongest model in our evaluation, achieves 71.1% exact-match accuracy on CurveBench-Easy and 28.7% on CurveBench-Hard. A Qwen3-VL-8B checkpoint trained using reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards reaches 31.7% on Easy, compared with 21.7% for its Thinking base model at a 16,384-token generation budget. The same comparison yields a gain of 1.1 percentage points on Hard.
author: Amirreza Mohseni, Mona Mohammadi, Morteza Saghafian, Naser Talebizadeh Sardari

title: Pause and Reflect: Conformal Aggregation for Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
content:
arXiv:2605.14098v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning with self-consistency improves performance by aggregating multiple sampled reasoning paths. In this setting, correctness is no longer tied to a single reasoning trace but to the aggregation rule over a pool of candidate paths, making aggregation uncertainty the central challenge. This issue is critical where confidently incorrect answers are far more costly than abstentions. We introduce a conformal procedure for CoT reasoning that directly addresses aggregation uncertainty. Our approach replaces majority voting with weighted score aggregation over reasoning paths and calibrates an abstention rule using conformal risk control. This approach leads to finite-sample guarantees on the confident-error rate--the probability that the system answers and is wrong. We further identify score separability as the key condition under which abstention provably improves selective accuracy, and derive closed-form expressions that predict accuracy gains from calibration data alone. The method is fully inference-time, and requires no retraining. Across four benchmarks, four open-source models, and three score classes, realized confident-error rates are consistent with the prescribed targets up to calibration-split and test-set variability. Our method achieves $90.1\%$ selective accuracy on GSM8K by abstaining on fewer than $5\%$ of problems, compared with $82.3\%$ accuracy under majority voting and $87.4\%$ under score-weighted voting without abstention, while conformal risk control keeps the expected rate of confidently wrong answers below $10\%$.
author: Yu Gu, Zijun Yu, Vahid Partovi Nia, Masoud Asgharian

title: On the Burden of Achieving Fairness in Conformal Prediction
content:
arXiv:2605.14260v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Conformal prediction is often calibrated with a single pooled threshold, but this can hide cross-group heterogeneity in score distributions and distort group-wise coverage. We study this phenomenon through the population score distributions underlying split conformal calibration. First, we derive a conservation law and lower bound showing that pooled calibration incurs irreducible group-wise coverage distortion at a scale set by cross-group quantile heterogeneity. Second, we demonstrate that the two leading fairness definitions for conformal prediction, Equalized Coverage and Equalized Set Size, are fundamentally in tension. Third, we quantify the cost of moving between policies which treat groups separately or pool them. Experiments on synthetic and real data confirm the same bidirectional trade-off after finite-sample calibration. Our results show that, for the policy families studied here, calibration choice does not remove cross-group heterogeneity; it determines whether the resulting distortion appears in the coverage or size dimension, providing a principled lens for analyzing fairness-oriented calibration choices in practice.
author: Ziang Gao, Pengqi Liu, Archer Yi Yang, Mouloud Belbahri, Jesse C. Cresswell, Masoud Asgharian

title: Imperfect World Models are Exploitable
content:
arXiv:2605.15960v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We propose a novel definition of model exploitation in reinforcement learning. Informally, a world model is exploitable if it implies that one policy should be strictly preferred over another while the environment's true transition model implies the reverse. We analogize our definition with a prior characterization of reward hacking but show that the associated proof of inevitability does not transfer to exploitation. To overcome this obstruction, we develop a general theory of reward hacking and model exploitation that proves that exploitation is essentially unavoidable on large policy sets and yields the corresponding claim for hacking as a special case. Unfortunately, we also find that the conditions that guarantee unhackability in finite policy sets have no counterpart that precludes exploitation. Consequently, we introduce a relaxed notion of exploitation and derive a safe horizon within which it can be avoided. Taken together, our results establish a formal bridge between reward hacking and model exploitation and elucidate the limits of safe planning in world models.
author: Logan Mondal Bhamidipaty, Esmeralda S. Whitammer, David Abel, Mykel J. Kochenderfer, Subramanian Ramamoorthy

title: Bayesian Optimization on Function Spaces via Sparse RKHS Manifolds
content:
arXiv:2610.07417v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Bayesian Optimization (BO) has become an established methodology for minimizing black-box functions of a vector input. Often, however, this parameter vector arises from the discretization of an inherently functional relationship. Several recent articles have considered the Functional Bayesian Optimization (FBO) setting, in which the variable to be optimized is not a member of a finite dimensional vector space, but rather an infinite dimensional function space. In this work, we propose $L^0$ Manifold Optimization (L0MO), a simple approach to FBO which searches the subset of a Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space (RKHS) consisting of functions with a sparse representation in the kernel functions, optimizing both the kernel locations and their coefficients. We discuss in detail the relationship between our method and existing ones, providing a unifying lens through which to view prior works. To assess our method against the state of the art, we conduct an extensive computational study, and along the way develop a novel set of benchmark test functions which port standard finite-dimensional ones to the infinite dimensional domain. Our experiments demonstrate that, on balance, the proposed method achieves superior performance across a wide range of test benchmarks.
author: Davide Sartor, Meghan E. Huber, Donghyun Kim, Nathan Wycoff

title: Anytime-Valid Runtime Monitoring of Learned Barrier Certificates
content:
arXiv:2610.27726v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Learned barrier certificates provide a principled mechanism for establishing safety of stochastic systems, but their validity may deteriorate during deployment when the underlying dynamics differ from those used for training. We propose an anytime-valid runtime monitor that audits a learned barrier certificate using observed closed-loop trajectories. The monitor is intended to detect loss of statistical support for the deployed barrier condition; it does not by itself guarantee detection before unsafe entry or safety of a subsequent intervention. Specifically, the conditional barrier-drift condition is formulated as an episode-wise sequential hypothesis test, and observed barrier increments are transformed into a nonnegative test supermartingale, yielding finite-sample false-alarm control under arbitrary stopping times. Inspired by finite-horizon safety verification, we further introduce a deterministic temporal shaping of the monitoring boundary, making the monitor more conservative early in a prescribed deployment horizon while preserving anytime-validity. The monitor is designed to detect statistical evidence that the safety certificate is no longer consistent with the observed dynamics, rather than to predict unsafe entry. To assess the monitor empirically, we evaluate empirical alarm behavior under valid and invalid certificates. Code and data are available at https://github.com/FormalCert-AI/runtime-barrier-monitor.
author: Zhipeng Cao, Taoran Wu, Weiru Cui, Luke Ong, Bai Xue

title: Recursive Semantic Divergence for LLM Agent Consistency
content:
arXiv:2610.33012v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents with tool use can behave inconsistently across independent runs from identical states. They may call different tools, produce contradictory outputs, or follow divergent strategies.This variability compounds over time and undermines deployment reliability. Existing evaluation metrics primarily measure task correctness via completion-based scores and do not capture consistency in agent behavior across executions. Separately, agent behavior is analyzed either at the token level using probability distributions or at the single-response level using semantic clustering, but neither captures how inconsistency propagates across future turns of a trajectory. We introduce Recursive Semantic Divergence (RSD), a trajectory-level consistency metric adapted from bisimulation metrics in reinforcement learning. RSD measures the expected cumulative semantic disagreement between two independent rollouts of the same agent from the same state, using natural language inference to detect logical inconsistency. It is defined recursively over future states and approximated by a neural network trained on independent rollouts. The learned metric estimates future divergence from the current state, providing a consistency score at each turn without requiring the full trajectory to complete. When used as a reward signal for fine-tuning, RSD reduces AUC coefficient of variation (CV) by up to 30.9% on tau2-bench and 50.5% on ToolSandbox. Across Qwen-2.5 and Qwen-3.5 models, RSD reduces AUC CV in seven out of eight model-benchmark settings, while improving the final task progress in all eight settings.
author: Harshavardhan Abichandani, Penny Chong, Atin Ghosh, Daniel Dahlmeier

title: Learning Pathology-Sensitive Representations for Unsupervised Retinal OCT Anomaly Detection
content:
arXiv:2610.33143v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Deep learning approaches for retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT) predominantly rely on predefined disease categories, limiting their ability to detect rare or previously unseen abnormalities. While visual foundation models provide transferable representations, their effectiveness in identifying pathological deviations from normal retinal anatomy remains insufficiently understood. In this work, we introduce an unsupervised framework for retinal OCT anomaly detection and localization that adapts pretrained visual representations to normal retinal anatomy through anatomy-aware reconstruction and contrastive triplet learning guided by synthetic structural perturbations, without requiring disease-specific annotations. We systematically investigate the influence of pretraining strategies, anatomy-aware representation adaptation, and anomaly scoring mechanisms on the detection and localization of unseen retinal abnormalities. Our findings demonstrate that adapting pretrained representations to normal retinal structure improves anomaly sensitivity, while pixel-space reconstruction errors and feature-space deviations provide complementary signals for identifying pathological changes. These findings underscore the importance of anatomy-aware representation learning and offer insights into developing generalizable retinal anomaly detection frameworks beyond predefined disease categories.
author: Tania Haghighi, Sina Gholami, Behafarin Emam, Jennifer I Lim, Theodore Leng, Atalie C Thompson, Hamed Tabkhi, Minhaj Nur Alam

title: How Much Do Structural Tools Help Small Coding Agents? A Pre-Registered Scale Study of Code Localization
content:
arXiv:2610.33958v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Code-graph and embedding tools are routinely added to LLM coding agents on the premise that they supply repository structure the model lacks. We report a pre-registered study of how much such tools help off-the-shelf agents localize the code an issue requires changing and how the benefit varies with model size. Nine open-weight models (Qwen3 0.6B to 32B, Gemma 4 E2B to 12B) run one fixed localization harness on 500 held-out SWE-bench tasks under four tool sets (grep only; plus embedding search; plus code-graph tools; both) and a placebo arm whose structural tools return random entities, with five sampled seeds per condition: 170,500 episodes under hypotheses, tests and claim criteria frozen before the runs. The tools raise canonical function Acc@10 by +0.06 to +0.10 for the Qwen3 models up to 14B and the two small Gemma 4 models, by +0.03 at 32B (a near miss after correction), and not at all for Gemma 4 12B, which rarely submits; the gain is larger for small models than for the largest model in both families. The placebo shows that the gain is caused by what the tools return rather than by having them, and that random tool output harms two small models. The pre-registered claim that a 4B model with tools matches a 32B model without them fails. Secondary analyses show that the embedding index, not the code graph, carries the gain; that the gain replicates on tasks created after every model's release and survives a shell harness, thinking mode, FP8 serving and a file-level metric that output formatting cannot inflate; and that it is mostly exposure: the tools show the gold code more often. Injecting the gold code directly explains the size trend. A 32B model already finds the code without the tools, so they add little exposure, while small models act on a shown answer less often (conversion 0.09, 0.24 and 0.40 at 1.7B, 4B and 32B). We release registration, code, episodes and analyses.
author: Saurav Bellam (The University of Texas at Austin)

title: Tree crown mortality and defoliation assessment in temperate forests using aerial imagery and deep learning
content:
Publication date: November 2026

Source: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation, Volume 154

Author(s): Mirela Beloiu, Elias Berger, Simon Ecke, Zhongyu Xia, Yixin Zhou, Cécile Reichmuth, Arthur Gessler, Hans-Joachim Klemmt, Jonas Glatthorn, Jonas Stillhard, Lars T. Waser, Verena C. Griess

title: S2IPNet: SAM 2-Guided Information Preservation Network for Infrared Small Target Detection
content: Infrared small target detection (IRSTD) remains challenging due to the extremely limited spatial extent of targets and the presence of complex background clutter. Existing deep learning methods often rely on strided convolution or pooling for downsampling, which inevitably leads to the loss of fine-grained spatial information. Meanwhile, although recent segmentation foundation models provide rich semantic priors, their direct application to IRSTD is hindered by domain discrepancies and feature misalignment. To address these issues, we propose a segment anything model (SAM) 2-guided information preservation network (S2IPNet), which is based on segmentation foundation model priors to guide information preservation in the convolutional representation paradigm. In particular, an information preservation encoder is designed to retain subtle spatial structures during downsampling by avoiding direct spatial sampling. A SAM 2-guided cross-attention fusion (SCAF) module is introduced to incorporate semantic priors into convolutional features through adaptive feature interaction. Furthermore, a supervised attention decoder with hierarchical exponential deep supervision (HEDS) progressively refines multiscale representations and stabilizes optimization. Extensive experiments on three datasets demonstrate that the proposed S2IPNet achieves superior performance compared with multiple state-of-the-art methods, particularly in comprehensive evaluation metrics such as F-measure, mean intersection over union (mIoU), and normalized IoU (nIoU). The code is available at https://github.com/haofan72/S2IPNet
author: Fan Hao, Feng Zhou, Pengfei Lu

title: Multiscale Characterization and Attribution of Earth's Oblateness Variations Using an SVMD–SSA Approach
content: Earth's oblateness variation (ΔJ2) is a key indicator of global-scale mass redistribution and Earth system dynamics. However, the coexistence of long-term, seasonal, interannual, and decadal signals, together with strong noise contamination and signal mixing, poses significant challenges for accurately characterizing its multiscale variability. Singular spectrum analysis (SSA) may have difficulty separating different temporal-scale components with comparable variance contributions, whereas successive variational mode decomposition (SVMD) is susceptible to noise-dominated modes and mode mixing. To overcome these limitations, an SVMD–SSA-based signal analysis approach integrating SVMD and SSA is proposed. Multisource satellite-derived geodetic datasets spanning 1976–2024, including satellite laser ranging observations and gravity recovery and climate experiment (GRACE)-derived gravity field solutions, are employed for multiscale analysis and geophysical attribution. Compared with empirical mode decomposition and discrete wavelet transform, SVMD provides clearer separation and reconstruction of the long-term, seasonal, interannual, and decadal components of ΔJ2, while SSA further identifies the dominant periodic signals within these temporal scales. The extracted long-term component reveals the transition of ΔJ2 from a steady decrease to a slowdown and subsequent reversal after 2002. Seasonal variability is dominated by terrestrial water storage, atmospheric pressure, and ocean mass redistribution, whereas interannual fluctuations exhibit strong associations with major climate modes, including El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO), Arctic Oscillation, Antarctic Oscillation, and Pacific Decadal Oscillation. Decadal variability further suggests potential links with solar activity and ENSO-related teleconnections. The proposed approach provides an effective tool for characterizing multiscale gravity-field variability and facilitates the investigation of Earth system mass redistribution using satellite geodetic observations.
author: Hongjuan Yu, Penglong Zhang, Yu Sun, Krzysztof Sośnica, Yong Zhang

title: Ensemble-EA and HS-SEA: Attention-Based Efficient Architectures With Bayesian Hyperparameter Optimization for RGB and Hyperspectral Remote Sensing Image Classification
content: Conventional deep learning models still face challenges from substantial intra-class variability, complex spatial structures, inter-class similarity, and high spectral dimensionality in hyperspectral imagery. To address these limitations, a unified remote sensing classification framework is proposed consisting of two complementary architectures: Ensemble-EA for RGB aerial scene classification and HS-SEA for hyperspectral image classification. The Ensemble-EA architecture integrates a truncated EfficientNet-B0 backbone, a self-attention mechanism, hierarchical feature learning, and ensemble decision refinement to capture local and global context in RGB imagery. For hyperspectral data, the proposed HS-SEA architecture introduces a Band Grouping Attention Module (BGAM) and a Spectral-to-Spatial Transfer Gate (SSTG) to exploit spectral-spatial dependencies while efficiently mitigating the Hughes phenomenon. Bayesian optimization is employed to optimize the downstream ensemble classifiers. The proposed framework is validated on nine benchmark datasets, including EuroSAT, NWPU-RESISC45, Bijie Landslide, Turkey Earthquake, MLRSNet, Indian Pines, Salinas, Pavia University, and the recently launched Geology-1 hyperspectral microsatellite dataset. Experimental results show superior classification performance across RGB and hyperspectral modalities, achieving overall accuracies of 6.75% on EuroSAT, 99.28% on NWPU, 93.31% on Bijie Landslide, 98.90% on Turkey Earthquake, 95.00% on MLRSNet, 99.15% on Indian Pines, 99.87% on Salinas, and 99.48% on Pavia University. On the labelscarce Geology-1 dataset, cross-site transfer learning using HS-SEA embeddings and a linear classifier trained on one site achieved 46% and 68% accuracy when transferred to two geographically distinct, unseen sites, demonstrating the framework's ability to generalize to novel, operationally relevant geological hyperspectral data. The results validate the framework's robustness, cross-modality generalization, and discriminative feature-learning effectiveness.
author: Muhammad Attique Khan, Muhammad Sami Ullah, Jiaxin Li, Majid Ali Khan, Saeed Iqbal, Latifah Almuqren, Muhammad John Abbas, Yunyoung Nam

title: Learning to Guide: An Adaptive Multisource Prompting and Geometric-Semantic Refinement Network for Remote Sensing Semantic Segmentation
content: Semantic segmentation of remote sensing images faces multiple challenges, including complex spatial structures, high intraclass variability, and insufficient cross-modal registration accuracy. Although foundation models, such as Segment Anything Model (SAM), exhibit strong generalizability, their direct application to remote sensing tasks is limited by their reliance on manual prompts and insufficient adaptation to domain-specific characteristics. To overcome these challenges, we propose an adaptive multisource prompting and geometric-semantic refinement network (MPGNet), which addresses complex spatial structures in remote sensing images through multidimensional guided reoptimization. First, we introduce a parameter-efficient adapter that integrates low-rank adaptation and snake-like linear layers into the SAM backbone to meticulously extract fine-grained textures and long-range dependencies from the RGB modality. Second, to handle complex topological variations, we design a dual-branch filtering module (using CNN and Transformer pathways) for the normalized digital surface model (nDSM). This module adaptively evaluates and selects the most reliable feature pathway and generates point and bounding box prompts without manual intervention. Third, RGB and nDSM features are synergistically fused through two complementary pathways: polygon boundary prompts for geometric structure refinement, and contrastive language-image pretraining text embeddings for robust semantic alignment. Finally, a hierarchical decoder integrates the aligned multimodal features with the generated spatial and semantic prompts to produce the final segmentation results. Extensive experiments on the Vaihingen and Potsdam datasets demonstrate that MPGNet outperforms various existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of mean accuracy and mean intersection over union, highlighting the superiority of combining multimodal automatic prompting with cross-modal geometric refinement.
author: Shenghao Qi, Weiwei Qiu, Liang Liao, Yuanyuan Liu, Wujie Zhou

title: Multihierarchical Mixed Cube Attention Interactive Network for Hyperspectral and Multispectral Image Fusion
content: To address the tradeoff between the spectral resolution and spatial resolution of hyperspectral images (HSIs), hyperspectral and multispectral image fusion (HSI-MSI) aims to generate a high-spatial-resolution hyperspectral image (HR-HSI) by integrating the spectral information of a hyperspectral image with the spatial details of a corresponding multispectral image (MSI). However, most existing methods overlook the inherent correlation between the spatial and spectral dimensions, limiting their joint exploitation of spatial and spectral information. In this study, a multihierarchical mixed cube attention interactive network (MMCAI-Net) is proposed, which considers this correlation and enhances the deep interaction across spatial and spectral dimensions in the HSI-MSI fusion process. The network primarily consists of a multihierarchical feature interaction stage and a gradual feature reconstruction stage, which are composed of the mixed cube attention interaction (MCAI) and cube feature aggregation and reconstruction (CFAR) modules, respectively. The MCAI module integrates global spatial and spectral information from the HSI and MSI through mixed cube attention, enabling cross-dimensional feature interaction. The CFAR module progressively aggregates these features to reconstruct an HR-HSI with enhanced spatial details and spectral fidelity. Experimental results on five datasets demonstrate that the MMCAI-Net method preserves more spatial and spectral details than seven literature methods, improving PSNR by 5% and reducing SAM by 8% compared with MCT-Net. These results suggest that the proposed method achieves superior HSI-MSI fusion results.
author: Huajing Wu, Wenjing Zhang, Kefei Zhang, Shuangshuang Shi, Fei Zhao, Lin Zhang, Lorenzo Bruzzone

title: A Pseudo-Random Coded Ground-Penetrating Radar for Glacier Thickness Detection
content: Accurately detecting and evaluating glacier thickness and ice reserves is of great significance for global climate change research and ecological environment protection of high frigid regions. A pseudorandom coded radar mounted on an uncrewed vehicle is developed to measure the subglacial topography and glacier thickness with high accuracy. Using the Golay complementary code as the transmitted signal and operating at the frequency range of 10–130 MHz with code length of 1024 bits, this radar system offers a range resolution of about 1.5 m in ice. The interleaved sampling of deep detection mode and shallow detection mode is used to improve the detection dynamic range of the system. In order to reduce the detection blind zone of deep mode, the pseudorandom encoded long pulse signal is divided into short pulses for transmission and reception, and the shift superposition is completed in the real-time processor to reduce the data rate of the radar. An IO pin of field programmable gate array is used to generate a pseudorandom encoded signal modulated by square carrier in series, which serves as the input source for the transmitter. A radio frequency switch in the receiving path is applied to prevent saturation of the receiver front-end and collect radar loop data as a reference signal for pulse compression. In addition, a frequency wavenumber domain migration algorithm is proposed to obtain a high processing gain and to improve the signal to noise ratio of the system. Field experiments at Bayi Glacier in northwestern China demonstrate clear imaging of ice-bedrock interfaces, while link-budget analysis suggests a potential detection capability of up to approximately 400 m under comparable ice-loss conditions.
author: Bo Zhao, Yan Liu, Shidong Li, Xiaojun Liu, Guangyou Fang

title: Lower Boundary-Aware Sky–Ground Segmentation for Robust Horizon Estimation in Low-Altitude UAV Remote Sensing
content: Low-altitude uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) provide flexible platforms for remote-sensing data acquisition, but their image sequences are frequently affected by attitude variation, illumination degradation, cluttered sky–ground structures, and partial occlusion. To improve horizon perception under these conditions, this article proposes LBA-YOLO-Seg, a lightweight lower boundary-aware sky–ground segmentation framework that explicitly links mask prediction with downstream geometric recoverability. The method combines Ghost-based feature extraction, Coordinate Attention, and a high-resolution boundary pathway to preserve boundary localization and directional continuity, while a boundary–completeness–adaptive Kalman estimator improves temporal stability. Experiments on a self-collected UAV dataset show that the proposed method outperforms traditional horizon detectors, representative segmentation networks, boundary-aware methods, and YOLO-family baselines in geometric accuracy and temporal stability. Zero-shot evaluation on the public CH1 dataset further demonstrates cross-domain generalization, while embedded deployment on Rhino Pi-X1 achieves an end-to-end processing rate of 47.53 FPS. These results indicate that optimizing segmentation representation for lower boundary recoverability provides an effective and deployable solution for robust UAV horizon perception.
author: Haonan Zhang, Wenyi Lin, Chuandong Guo, Lijia Cao, Huali Gou, Jiajun Li, Jinhui Li

title: Deep Learning-Enabled Identification Dominant Species in Harmful Algal Blooms Using Broadband Satellite Data
content: Harmful algal blooms (HABs), are worldwide marine ecological disasters marked by diverse dominant species. Identifying these species is critical due to their differing ecological impacts and toxicity. The broadband optical satellites offer advantages for monitoring fine-scale nearshore HABs. However, most of them have low spectral resolution and few bands, which poses a significant challenge to accurate species identification. To address these issues, this study developed a deep learning-based framework for identifying HABs dominant species (RT-SGINet). The framework integrates a spectral feature transfer-based sample generation strategy to produce high-quality 3-D red tide samples, alleviating the uneven distribution of species-specific training data. The dominant species identification module based on cross-spatial feature fusion was developed to enhance interspecies separability by jointly extracting spectral and spatial-structural features. Furthermore, a student–teacher semisupervised learning strategy was introduced to improve generalizability across different species distributions. The experimental results demonstrated that the sample generation module preserves high spatial-spectral fidelity, enabling precise species identification in few-shot scenarios. RT–SGINet accurately identifies three dominant species, including Akashiwo sanguinea in the East China Sea, red Noctiluca scintillans, and green Noctiluca scintillans, with an overall accuracy of 94.5%. Compared with existing methods, RT-SGINet significantly improves the identification accuracy by 3.52%–8.66%. The model exhibited strong generalization capabilities across various areas and broadband satellite sensors. This study provides a generalizable deep learning framework for fine-grained HAB species identification under spectrally limited and sample-imbalanced conditions.
author: Xin Zhao, Yanfang Xiao, Yi Ma, Yujie Chen, Wei Zhao, Na Liu, Baohua Shan, Manli Zhou, Rongjie Liu

title: Exploiting CNN and ViT Strengths: Local and Global Feature Fusion for Enhanced Remote Sensing Super-Resolution
content: The transmission and compression of remote sensing images often require reduced spatial resolution to improve bandwidth and storage efficiency, motivating the reconstruction of high-quality images from low-resolution inputs. To simulate this degradation, we generate low-resolution images using bicubic downsampling. Vision Transformers (ViTs) capture long-range dependencies for recovering global terrain structures, while convolutional neural networks (CNNs) effectively preserve local textures and structural details. Accordingly, we propose a dual-stream architecture that integrates ViT and CNN features through a bidirectional feature fusion module, which alleviates the representation discrepancy between ViT patch features and convolutional feature maps. By jointly exploiting global context and local details, the proposed method enables coherent reconstruction of large-scale landscapes and fine-grained infrastructure. Extensive experiments on satellite image super-resolution datasets with different spatial resolutions demonstrate its effectiveness in recovering high-frequency details and preserving critical geospatial information.
author: Chenghao Qiu, Aiping Ye, Cong Lin, Xu Cheng

title: Explainable CyGNSSnet: Deep-Learning Retrieval of Global GNSS-R Soil Moisture
content: Global navigation satellite system reflectometry (GNSS-R) enables high-revisit soil moisture (SM) monitoring, but retrieval over land remains confounded by vegetation, roughness, and topography. We present explainable CyGNSSnet, a hybrid deep-learning retrieval that fuses the full Cyclone GNSS (CYGNSS) delay-Doppler maps (DDMs) and derived observables with daily moderate resolution imaging spectroradiometer optical/thermal indices and static topographic, biomass, and eco-climatic descriptors. The model is trained on 2019–2020 data, with soil moisture active passive (SMAP) L3 soil moisture as the reference, and tested on the fully independent year 2021 and against International Soil Moisture Network (ISMN) stations. CyGNSSnet reaches a correlation coefficient $R=0.90$ and a root mean square error $\text{RMSE}=0.046\,\mathrm{m^{3}\,m^{-3}}$ on the 2021 test set. In addition, a SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) audit shows a physically consistent retrieval: the GNSS-R amplitude metrics provide the sensitivity to the soil dielectric properties, and hence, to soil moisture; vegetation indices and biomass carry the vegetation conditioning; and DDM attributions concentrate near the quasi-specular core. Relative to an auxiliary-only model with no CYGNSS input, the GNSS-R observables remove 25% of the error variance and raise the per-cell temporal correlation from 0.35 to 0.51: they mainly supply the temporal (wetting–drying) signal of soil moisture, while the auxiliaries reproduce the time-mean spatial pattern. Triple collocation at the ISMN stations bounds the SM random error at the SMAP level ($\sim 0.03\,\mathrm{m^{3}\,m^{-3}}$, a lower bound because CyGNSSnet is trained on SMAP). A SMAP-enhanced control that adds SMAP-derived vegetation water content and optical depth, as often done in the literature, improves RMSE by only $0.004\,\mathrm{m^{3}\,m^{-3}}$, yet SHAP shows these inputs dominating its attribution, a fingerprint of input–target coupling that justifies their exclusion. Requiring no SMAP-derived input at inference time, Explainable CyGNSSnet can be retrained on other GNSS-R missions, such as HydroGNSS and support soil-moisture monitoring beyond the SMAP era.
author: Hamed Izadgoshasb, Luke J. Pugin, Tianqi Xiao, Nazzareno Pierdicca, Jens Wickert, Milad Asgarimehr

title: SpectralDualIGANet: A Spectral-Prior-Guided Dual-Gated Segmentation Network for Fine-Grained Segmentation of Aquatic Invasive Plants
content: Floating aquatic invasive plants, represented by water hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes), can rapidly form extensive surface coverage in inland water bodies such as lakes and reservoirs, leading to substantial ecological and economic losses. Therefore, efficient, fine-grained, and continuous dynamic monitoring is urgently needed. uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) remote sensing provides high-resolution observations for such surveys. However, in complex aquatic environments, aquatic invasive plants are prone to spectral and textural confusion with riparian vegetation, water shadows, and surrounding backgrounds. Moreover, slight spatial misalignment between RGB and multispectral imagery may further weaken the effectiveness of cross-modal feature fusion. To address these challenges, this study proposes SpectralDualIGANet, a spectral-prior-guided dual-gated segmentation network for fine-grained segmentation of aquatic invasive plants. The proposed method employs a learnable spectral alignment module to compensate for cross-modal spatial offsets and transforms physically meaningful spectral indices, including NDVI, NDRE, and NDWI, into learnable priors. These priors are then used to guide feature modulation through a dual-gating mechanism, thereby enhancing target responses while suppressing interference from complex backgrounds. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms mainstream unimodal and multimodal approaches under random split testing and maintains stable performance in a within-lake cross-region transfer test between two spatially separated subregions of the same lake system. Specifically, under complex background conditions, the proposed method achieves an IoU of 94.66% and a Dice coefficient of 97.25% for water hyacinth segmentation, while maintaining an IoU above 91% in within-lake cross-region testing. Overall, the proposed method provides reliable technical support for coverage estimation and dynamic monitoring of aquatic invasive plants.
author: Xiaomei Yi, Jie Wang, Lufeng Mo, Guoying Wang, Peng Wu

title: NSCAT5: A Geophysical Model Function for Space-Borne Ku-band Scatterometers, Including SST Dependence
content: This study investigates the incidence-angle dependence of sea surface temperature (SST) effects on Ku-band scatterometer normalized radar cross section (NRCS) and develops a generalized SST-dependent geophysical model function (GMF), referred to as NSCAT-5. Unlike previous SST-dependent Ku-band GMFs developed for individual fixed-incidence-angle scatterometers, NSCAT-5 extends the SST correction to a broader incidence-angle range for multimission Ku-band wind retrievals. Winds retrieved from the C-band scatterometer onboard the ERS-2 satellite (ESCAT) and onboard MetOp satellite (ASCAT), whose SST dependence is negligible compared with Ku-band winds, are used as SST-insensitive transfer references. Analysis of collocated ESCAT–NSCAT data and physics-based radar backscatter simulations shows that SST effects on Ku-band NRCS increase approximately linearly with incidence angle and become weak at low incidence angles. Reference SST correction coefficients are derived from closely collocated ASCAT and HY-2C scatterometer data and generalized through incidence-angle interpolation. Validation with NSCAT, RapidScat, ScatSat-1, HY-2 HY-2 series scatterometers, and WindRAD demonstrates that NSCAT-5 substantially reduces systematic SST-dependent wind speed biases, with the maximum SST-induced bias over the 0 °C–30 °C SST range reduced from more than 1.3 m/s to below 0.2 m/s. These results improve the consistency of multimission Ku- and C-band scatterometer winds and support integrated ocean surface wind applications.
author: Zhixiong Wang, Juhong Zou, Qian Feng, Ad Stoffelen, Xiao-Ming Li, Anton Verhoef, Huimin Li

title: VLM-Guided Lightweight Multitask Framework for Pine Wilt Disease Quantitative Assessment in UAV Remote Sensing
content: Pine wilt disease (PWD) is a highly destructive and contagious forest disease, posing a serious threat to forest ecological security and sustainable forestry development. Under complex stand structures and limited resources, existing methods fail to balance localization accuracy, quantification precision, and semantic understanding of disease distribution. To address this issue, we propose a multitask learning-based model, named PWD multitask network (PWD-MTNet26). Furthermore, a vision-language model-guided semantic-prior enhancement strategy is introduced at training time. By constructing an offline teacher package containing region masks, boundary cues, and confidence information, selective distillation is imposed on the segmentation branch, enabling high-level semantic priors to refine disease-region delineation without increasing inference cost. A joint loss function is constructed to integrate detection and segmentation losses into a unified framework, with optimization conducted at both the pixel and region levels, which improves the recognition of early-stage disease with weak features. Experimental results on real-world datasets show that PWD-MTNet26-SPG achieves 93.5% mAP$_{50}$ for detection and 87.6% mIoU for segmentation. With only 2.5M parameters, the model achieves an inference speed of 84 FPS under the specified hardware and input settings. In the damaged area estimation task, the proposed method outperforms comparative methods across multiple metrics, reducing the normalized root-mean-square error to 0.2197 and the mean absolute error to 1.8149 m$^{2}$, while the damage rate error is only −0.69%.
author: Lina Wang, Wei William Wang, Junchao Yuan, Yuchao Xia, Kai Fang, Dalei Song, Hailin Feng

title: Multifrequency Microwave Signatures of Layered Soil Moisture and Temperature Profile Variations Using an NMM3D-VIE-DDA Model
content: This study investigates how depth-dependent variations in soil moisture and temperature affect active and passive microwave simulated observables using a full-wave NMM3D-VIE-DDA model. Baseline profiles are constructed from in situ measurements in Saihanba (Hebei, China), and profile scenarios are generated to represent variations concentrated in the shallow (0 cm), middle (3 cm), and deep (5 cm) layers, together with piecewise-constant approximations. Simulations are performed at 1.26 and 6.925 GHz for incidence angles of $30^\circ$, $40^\circ$, and $50^\circ$, with convergence at 6.925 GHz assessed using $n_{r} = 15$ Monte Carlo realizations of statistically generated rough surfaces. Across the tested cases, profile scenarios with shallow-layer variations produce the largest changes in backscattering, interferometric phase, and brightness temperature, whereas scenarios with middle- and deep-layer variations have weaker effects. A key contribution is the interferometric analysis: phase separability is stronger at 1.26 GHz than at 6.925 GHz, with coherence remaining high ($>0.99$), supporting stable phase interpretation. Meanwhile, the coherence with respect to soil moisture variations exhibits a roughness and frequency dependent pattern. For passive simulated observations, polarization and frequency jointly control sensitivity: V/H brightness-temperature contrast increases with observation angle from 30$^{\circ }$ to 50$^{\circ }$, and the strongest correlation with the simulated brightness temperature shifts from the 0–20 cm mean soil temperature at 1.26 GHz to the 0–3 cm mean soil temperature at 6.925 GHz. A practically important result is that piecewise-constant profiles at 1 cm resolution interval and continuous profiles produce closely matched responses in both active and passive channels under the tested setup, supporting simplified layered parameterization for retrieval-oriented modeling within a validated domain. The results provide bounded, physically consistent guidance for multichannel retrieval algorithm design, and the main qualitative conclusions remain valid under several additional reference roughness conditions considered in this study.
author: Shaojie Xu, Jiancheng Shi, Shurun Tan

title: Lightweight Remote-Sensing Image Super- Resolution via Uncertainty-Guided Contextual Token Aggregation Network
content: Recent advances in remote sensing image super-resolution (RSISR) have achieved remarkable progress. However, restoring fine structural details in complex scenes and efficiently modeling spatial heterogeneity remain challenging. In addition, many existing methods rely on computationally expensive dense global interactions, which limits their practical applicability in resource-constrained scenarios. To address these issues, we propose an Uncertainty-Guided Contextual Token Aggregation Network (UCTAN) for RSISR. The proposed network consists of two key designs. First, a Contextualized Aggregation Block (CAB) is introduced to cluster spatial tokens into compact contextual representations, enabling efficient and stable contextual token aggregation. This design reduces redundant computation while enhancing the modeling of local details and global structures. Second, an Uncertainty-Guided Token Interaction module is developed to exploit local uncertainty information estimated from feature variance, which complementarily guides contextual interaction and spatial refinement, thereby improving the adaptive modeling capability of the network for complex regions and high-frequency details. Extensive experiments demonstrate that UCTAN achieves superior or competitive performance on multiple remote sensing datasets and attains a favorable balance between reconstruction quality and computational complexity, validating its effectiveness and practical value for real-world RSISR tasks.
author: Yongxin Liu, Shuli Cheng, Liejun Wang, Yikemaiti Sataer

title: Controlling Unreliable Observation Propagation in Satellite-Video Multiobject Tracking via Candidate Refinement and Short-Window Trajectory Rectification
content: High-resolution optical satellite video enables persistent wide-area observation. However, robust multiobject tracking remains highly challenging because small moving targets typically occupy only a few pixels and generate weak, temporally unstable responses that are easily confused with background clutter. Preserving such faint targets usually requires a recall-oriented strategy that retains low-confidence candidates. Once integrated into data association, these unreliable observations tend to propagate errors through matching and state updating, resulting in false trajectories, identity switches, and fragmentation. To address the conflict between weak-target preservation and unreliable-observation propagation, this article proposes a preserve–rectify–maintain tracking framework with two complementary components: weak-observation-oriented front-end refinement (WOFR) and spatio-temporal trajectory rectification and cascade tracking (STRC). A WOFR enhances target-background discriminability through representation-level temporal reweighting and improves response-map reliability through constrained heatmap correction, thereby improving candidate quality while retaining sensitivity to weak targets. An STRC implements trajectory-level rectification and maintenance by screening refined candidates through short-window global consistency reasoning, removing unsupported observations, and passing the rectified observations to a lightweight online tracker for efficient long-term association and state maintenance. By limiting the propagation of unreliable observations under weak-observation conditions, the proposed framework improves the balance between recall and tracking robustness. Experiments on the VISO and SATMTB-multiobject tracking (MOT) datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. On VISO, the method achieves 71.2% MOTA and 79.7% IDF1, outperforming the compared methods on both metrics. On SATMTB-MOT, it achieves the best MOTA and IDF1 for the airplane and car categories.
author: Fen Hu, Peng Yang, Jie Dou, Lei Dou

title: Mitigating Information Loss and Enhancing Representation for Small-Object Detection in Remote Sensing
content: Small-object detection in remote sensing imagery remains a highly challenging task. Small object detection in remote sensing imagery is limited by two coupled effects: target evidence is progressively weakened by repeated downsampling, whereas high-resolution features preserve object boundaries but also amplify clutter. To address these challenges, this article proposes a novel detection network, termed MILER, built upon the FCOS framework. MILER is designed to mitigate information loss and enhance small object representations through two key components: the feature reconstruction (FR) module and the local-global feature enhancement (LGFE) module. Specifically, FR projects ground-truth boxes onto the $P2$ and $P3$ grids and requires the corresponding features to reconstruct scale-aligned binary target masks. This target-aware auxiliary task strengthens supervision for tiny-object spatial evidence. This module is discarded during inference and, therefore, introduces no additional computational overhead. Meanwhile, the LGFE operates on $P2$ and constructs a spatially normalized pixel-aware context map to modulate multireceptive-field local responses, thereby strengthening fine object structures under global contextual guidance without indiscriminately amplifying shallow features. Extensive experiments are conducted on four representative remote sensing small-object detection benchmarks, namely AI-TOD-v2, SODA-A, LEVIR-SHIP, and RS-STOD. The proposed MILER achieves 27.5% AP on AI-TOD-v2, 29.0% AP$\mathrm{_{rS}}$ on SODA-A, 86.4% AP$\mathrm{_{50}}$ on LEVIR-SHIP, 76.7% mAP$_{0.5}$ on RS-STOD, outperforming the baseline methods and demonstrating its effectiveness for remote sensing small-object detection.
author: Fenhua Wang, Liufeng Li, Ziyi Liu, Hongmin Liu, Zekai Shao

title: Frequency-Relation Guided Historical Inversion for Raw-Exemplar-Free Continual Hyperspectral Image Classification
content: Raw-exemplar-free continual hyperspectral image (HSI) classification aims to learn newly introduced land-cover classes while retaining old-class discrimination without storing historical HSI patches. In this work, raw-exemplar-free denotes a compact-memory-assisted setting in which no historical HSI patches, pixel-level spectral-spatial tensors, spatial coordinates, or persistent generated samples are retained; only compact noninput statistics and normalized feature references are used for reconstruction guidance and memory calibration. The main challenge is to construct historical evidence that is structurally faithful, discriminative, and consistent with the evolving feature space. To address this challenge, this article proposes a frequency-relation guided structured historical inversion framework, termed FR-SHI. Frequency-relation guided historical reconstruction reconstructs old-class auxiliary samples by combining frequency structural constraints with relation-memory guidance. Old-new collaborative relational distillation preserves both output responses and channel-spatial feature relations of the previous model, while temporal drift suppression and calibration suppresses representation drift and calibrates compact historical memories after each task. Experiments on Houston, Salinas, and WHU-Hi-LongKou show that FR-SHI provides more stable old-class retention and better final classification performance than representative raw-exemplar-free continual learning methods. Compared with the closest raw-exemplar-free HSI-specific inversion baseline, HyperSC, FR-SHI improves final OA by 3.58, 0.88, and 3.91 percentage points on Houston, Salinas, and WHU-Hi-LongKou, respectively.
author: Haibin Wu, Xing Chen, Siqi Yan, Minhui Wang, Aili Wang, Gabor Molnar

title: Tropospheric NO2 Retrieval From the FY-3F OMS-N Instrument: First Results and Validation
content: The ozone monitoring suite-Nadir (OMS-N), a hyperspectral ultraviolet-visible instrument aboard the Fengyun-3F (FY-3F) satellite, was launched in August 2023 into a morning Sun-synchronous orbit. As a state-of-the-art payload, OMS-N provides high-resolution (7 km × 7 km) observations of global atmospheric composition, filling a critical gap in morning atmospheric trace gas monitoring. Nitrogen dioxide (NO2) is a key atmospheric trace gas with significant impacts on air quality and atmospheric chemistry. Currently, high-resolution satellite observations are largely restricted to afternoon overpasses, which limits the ability to characterize morning emission impacts. Here, we present the first retrieval and validation of tropospheric NO2 vertical column densities from OMS-N measurements using a differential optical absorption spectroscopy based approach. To enhance computational efficiency and address nonlinear radiative transfer effects, a machine-learning-assisted air mass factor scheme is implemented, incorporating high-resolution GEOS-CF profiles as a priori constraints. Comparisons with TROPOspheric Monitoring Instrument and GOME-2C measurements demonstrate strong consistency, with correlation coefficients ranging from 0.77 to 0.94 and RMSE values of 1.01–2.85 × 1015 molecules/cm2 in representative polluted regions. Validation against Pandora observations further confirms the retrieval capability, with correlation coefficients of 0.80 at urban sites and 0.84 at suburban sites. These results highlight the distinct capability of the FY-3F OMS-N to characterize high-resolution morning tropospheric NO2 distributions, offering critical insights into diurnal emission patterns and atmospheric chemistry.
author: Yichen Li, Chao Yu, Huanhuan Yan, Jing Fan, Wenwu Wang, Ying Zhang, Jinhua Tao, Husi Letu, Liangfu Chen

title: An Integrated Spatial–Temporal Framework for Annual Forest Canopy Height Mapping Using Fused GEDI and ICESat-2 Data
content: Forest canopy height (FCH) is essential for characterizing forest vertical structure and supporting biomass, carbon-stock, and ecosystem assessments. This study developed a framework for annual FCH mapping in Heilongjiang Province, China, from 2020 to 2024 by integrating consistency-corrected GEDI and ICESat-2/ATL08 observations with optical, synthetic aperture radar, topographic, and climatic variables. A multiscale attention convolutional neural network with center feature fusion (MSA-CNN-CF) was first used for spatially continuous FCH retrieval, followed by graph-based residual diffusion (Graph-RD) to reduce spatially structured errors. Compared with a conventional CNN, MSA-CNN-CF increased the average $R^{2}$ from 0.54 to 0.61 and reduced RMSE from 5.07 to 4.20 m. Graph-RD further increased the average $R^{2}$ to 0.70 and reduced RMSE to 3.58 m. An adaptive spatio-temporal trend constraint (ASTC) method was then used to retrospectively reconstruct the missing 2023 FCH map. In a simulated missing-year experiment, ASTC achieved an $R^{2}$ of 0.92 and an RMSE of 1.52 m in stable undisturbed forests. In forests disturbed in 2022, ASTC achieved an RMSE of 3.62 m, representing a 47.96% reduction relative to linear interpolation. The proposed framework improves the spatial continuity and temporal completeness of regional FCH products and provides a practical basis for forest structural monitoring and carbon assessment.
author: Guanran Wang, Ying Yu, Xiguang Yang, Hanyuan Dong, Xuebing Guan, Hang Xu

title: BGA-YOLO: Bilinear Gated Attention for Lightweight and Real-Time Multiscale Object Detection
content: Remote sensing object detection remains challenging due to extreme scale variation, cluttered backgrounds, and the need for low-latency inference under practical computing constraints. Although recent lightweight designs aim to improve the accuracy–efficiency tradeoff, achieving reliable performance across diverse scenes while maintaining efficient inference remains nontrivial. To address this issue, we propose bilinear gated attention (BGA)-YOLO, a compact detector for real-time optical aerial object detection. Its BGA module adopts a dual-path design that separates semantic refinement from detail preservation for dense and tiny targets. Extensive experiments on five benchmarks (NWPU VHR-10, satellite imagery multivehicles dataset, DOTA-v1.0, VEDAI, and RTTS) verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. Compared with the baseline YOLOv8n (and YOLOv8n-oriented-bounding-box (OBB) for DOTA-v1.0), the proposed BGA-YOLO (and BGA-OBB) improves mAP$_{50}$ by +1.61%, +2.44%, and +0.76%, and mAP$_{50:95}$ by +3.23%, +2.81%, and +1.29%, on NWPU VHR-10, DOTA-v1.0, and SIMD, respectively. Additional evaluations show gains of +2.16%/+1.38% and +0.74%/+0.86% (mAP$_{50}$/mAP$_{50:95}$) on VEDAI under tiny-object conditions and RTTS under hazy conditions. Furthermore, BGA-YOLO maintains highly efficient operation, recording a model-level inference speed of 274.3 FPS and demonstrating a full inference pipeline latency of only 22.10 ms/source MP on real remote sensing images, establishing a favorable accuracy–latency tradeoff.
author: Wei Qian, Jiaqi Liu, Siqi Chen, Yonghua Li, Zhenyi Xu, Jianming Wei

title: DviCD: Lightweight Multiscale Calibration for High-Resolution Remote Sensing Change Detection
content: Remote sensing change detection (RSCD) aims to identify land-cover changes from bitemporal images while suppressing pseudo changes caused by illumination variations, seasonal differences, and viewpoint shifts. However, lightweight RSCD models still face challenges in multiscale feature interaction and boundary preservation. To address these issues, we propose DviCD, a lightweight Siamese network based on HRNetW18 with a hierarchical multiscale calibration framework. The network maintains high-resolution representations throughout feature extraction and introduces progressive feature calibration to enhance semantic guidance for shallow features. Specifically, a dual variation alignment (DVA) module is designed to model bitemporal feature inconsistencies from a dual-branch perspective. It decomposes bitemporal discrepancies into complementary change and consistency representations, followed by adaptive alignment to suppress unreliable variations while preserving discriminative change cues. Furthermore, a cross-scale (DVA) module is introduced to perform cross-scale feature calibration, enabling effective integration of local structural details and high-level semantic context. To further improve spatial precision, a lightweight details injection module is employed to recover boundary information lost during feature aggregation and enhance fine-grained structural awareness. Extensive experiments on the LEVIR-CD, WHU-CD, and SYSU-CD datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method. DviCD achieves 85.60% Intersection over Union and 92.24% F1-score on LEVIR-CD with only 18.49M parameters and 15.63 GFLOPs, achieving a favorable tradeoff between accuracy and efficiency.
author: Guangping Li, Zhenxuan He, Jing Ling, Di Dong

title: QL-Sec: Quantum AI-Enabled Security Framework for LLM-Driven Low-Altitude Remote Sensing Networks
content: Low-altitude remote sensing network technology has advanced rapidly, especially with the assistance of large language models (LLMs). The use of LLMs, especially with autonomous aerial vehicles in remote sensing systems, poses significant security and privacy risks due to the need to transmit sensitive information and to enable large-scale distributed communication. This article introduces the quantum AI security (QL-Sec) framework for LLM-powered low-altitude remote sensing networks. The proposed solution utilizes a hybrid QL-Sec mechanism designed to enhance confidentiality, integrity, and authentication, and to resist adversarial intrusions. The framework also uses quantum-secured encryption and privacy-preserving feature perturbation to help reduce information leakage during edge–cloud communication. Results reveal that the proposed framework achieves 96.41% attack detection accuracy, a secret key rate of 0.91 bits/use, and a reduced quantum bit error rate of 0.029. Shapley additive explanations explainability analysis validates the contribution of quantum-secure and quantum-safe components to trustworthy decision-making. The proposed quantum AI-based system provides an efficient, scalable, and highly secure solution for future intelligent low-altitude remote sensing systems.
author: Wajdan Al Malwi, Hussam Al Hamadi, Abdulrahman Mohammed Alamoudi, Nazik Alturki, Fatima Asiri, Fahad Masood

title: HyperInfer: Accelerating Large Language Model Inference via Importance-Informed Prefix-KV Caching and Prefetching
content: Modern advanced large language model (LLM) applications often prepend long contexts before user queries to improve model output quality. These contexts frequently repeat, either partially or fully, across multiple queries. Existing systems typically store and reuse the keys and values of these contexts (referred to as prefix KVs) to reduce redundant computation and time to first token (TTFT). When prefix KVs need to be stored on disks due to insufficient CPU memory, reusing them does not always reduce TTFT, as disk I/O latency is high. In this paper, we present HyperInfer, an importance-informed multi-tier prefix KV caching and prefetching system designed to reduce TTFT in LLM inference. HyperInfer first employs an I/O-efficient algorithm to identify and load only the most important KVs, thereby minimizing I/O overhead. Then, to further hide loading latency, it leverages the inter-layer similarity of token importance to speculatively prefetch the next layer’s critical KVs during the current layer’s computation. Finally, HyperInfer optimizes prefix-KV storage and cache utilization via importance-informed KV placement, further reducing TTFT in end-to-end inference. Our experimental results show that HyperInfer can reduce TTFT by up to 1.75$\boldsymbol{\times}$× compared to state-of-the-art systems, while maintaining comparable inference accuracy.
author: Ruidong Zhang, Weijian Chen, Ping Chen, Shuibing He, Wenjie Liang, Rongchen Liu, Siling Yang, Xuechen Zhang

title: Layer-Wise Principal Gradient Compression for Distributed Machine Learning
content: Distributed Machine Learning (DML) can accelerate model training by using multiple training nodes and large datasets. As model and data sizes grow, DML often uses more training nodes, and frequent model information exchange creates high communication overhead. To reduce this overhead, we propose PrincipalCatcher, a layer-wise gradient compression method based on Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and error feedback. PrincipalCatcher uses PCA to capture the main gradient components in each layer and transmits only the compressed gradient representation during iterative training. To limit the accuracy loss caused by lossy compression, each worker accumulates compression errors and adds them to gradients in the next epoch. We evaluate PrincipalCatcher on image classification tasks under distributed training settings. The results show that PrincipalCatcher can reduce gradient transmission by up to 96.4% while keeping accuracy close to conventional stochastic gradient descent in most tested settings.
author: Zehua Guo, Jiaxin Tan, Chao Yao, Yuying Li

title: Hardware Implementation and Security Analysis of Local-Masked NTT for CRYSTALS-Kyber
content: The rapid evolution of post-quantum cryptography, spurred by standardization efforts such as those by NIST, has highlighted the prominence of lattice-based cryptography, notably exemplified by CRYSTALS/Kyber. However, concerns persist regarding the security of cryptographic implementations, particularly in the face of Side-Channel Analysis (SCA). The usage of operations like the Number Theoretic Transform (NTT) in CRYSTALS/Kyber introduces vulnerabilities to SCA attacks, especially single-trace attacks, such as soft-analytical side-channel attacks (SASCA). To address this threat, Ravi et al. proposed local masking as a countermeasure by randomizing the NTT’s twiddle factors, but its implementation and security implications require further investigation. This paper presents a hardware implementation of an NTT with local masking, evaluating its performance, area utilization, and security implications. Additionally, it analyzes the vulnerabilities inherent in local masking and assesses its practical security effectiveness through non-specific t-tests, showing that there are configurations of local masking that are more prone to leakage than others.
author: Rafael Carrera Rodriguez, Emanuele Valea, Florent Bruguier, Pascal Benoit

title: Full-Chip Thermal Monitoring in Silicon-Photonic Chiplet Systems: Repurposing the Photonic Interposer Network
content: Integration of Silicon-Photonic (SiPh) interconnects with multi-chiplet systems offers unprecedented bandwidth and energy efficiency for next-generation computing. However, the resulting high power density and complex vertical thermal coupling create severe thermal challenges that threaten both computational integrity and photonic communication reliability. Accurate and efficient full-chip thermal monitoring is a critical prerequisite for dynamic thermal management, yet it remains challenging. The limited number of physical thermal sensors that are often sparsely placed on the compute chiplets fails to capture the intricate 3D thermal landscape, especially within the photonic interposer network (PIN) itself. To this end, we propose TherMoPIN, a novel framework achieving accurate yet cost-effective full-chip thermal monitoring. In addition to the physical thermal sensors that are readily placed on chiplets, it repurposes the existing PIN into a uniformly placed virtual thermal sensor array with negligible cost increases. TherMoPIN comprises two key enablers. First, we propose ArbLink, a precise and cost-efficient thermal sensing mechanism, which transforms the entire PIN into a dense and uniformly-distributed ‘virtual’ sensor array by reusing available photonic routers for thermal sensing, with minimal hardware overhead. Second, we develop HorVer, a lightweight thermal reconstruction technique that fuses sparse, direct readings from horizontal on-chiplet thermal sensors (i.e., physical ones) with the dense, indirect thermal data from the vertical photonic interposer network (i.e., virtual ones), capturing and modeling the critical thermal coupling between the compute chiplets and the photonic interposer. This unique horizontal-vertical data fusion allows HorVer to accurately reconstruct the full-chip thermal map of SiPh-chiplet systems. Experimental results demonstrate that TherMoPIN achieves high thermal monitoring accuracy, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods that rely solely on physical sensors. Furthermore, it accomplishes this with negligible additional hardware cost, as it primarily reuses the already-present photonic infrastructure for sensing.
author: Mengquan Li, Yangfan Li, Zhaoyuan Zhang, Zhengjie Jin, Shu Li, Cen Chen, Kenli Li

title: Ps-Stream: Proactive Straggler Mitigation Using Spatio-Temporal Features for Elastic Stream Computing Systems
content: Recent stream computing systems have shifted from static, threshold-based straggler detection to adaptive, temporal-pattern-based prediction. Existing prediction approaches typically rely on autoregressive time-series analysis to model each node’s historical resource usage within a cluster. However, they often overlook cross-node state correlations, resulting in isolated prediction models that fail to capture the dynamic spatio-temporal dependencies among nodes. To address these limitations, we propose Ps-Stream, a proactive framework for straggler prediction and mitigation. First, Ps-Stream constructs a unified spatio-temporal graph by modeling compute nodes as a spatial graph at each time step and linking each node across adjacent time steps. Second, it learns spatio-temporal representations for straggler prediction by combining Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) to capture spatial dependencies with attention mechanisms to model temporal dynamics. Third, it incorporates a fine-grained task migration strategy that proactively reallocates tasks from predicted stragglers to the least-loaded nodes while considering task dependencies and migration costs to minimize migration overhead. Experimental results show that Ps-Stream improves straggler prediction accuracy by up to 26%, reduces maximum system latency by 62%, more than doubles maximum throughput, and improves resource utilization by up to 34% compared with state-of-the-art baselines.
author: Minghui Wu, Dawei Sun, Shang Gao, Keqin Li, Rajkumar Buyya

title: LevelKV: Hierarchical KV Cache Pruning for Efficient and Reliable LLM Inference
content: The performance and functionality of large language model (LLM)-based applications heavily depend on their contextual inputs. As applications become more sophisticated, their contexts grow increasingly complex, leading to two critical challenges: (i) excessive computational and memory overhead—particularly from the key-value (KV) cache—and (ii) heightened security risks arising from heterogeneous and unverified context sources. Existing approaches fail to address both issues simultaneously: context compression methods often discard crucial information, undermining instruction fidelity, while security-oriented defenses typically introduce additional computational costs. We present LevelKV, a hierarchical KV cache pruning framework that achieves efficient and reliable LLM inference. LevelKV employs a holistic metric to jointly identify critical activations in both Key and Value caches, and introduces a hierarchy-preserving mechanism that structurally prioritizes high-privilege prompts during pruning to maintain reliability. Evaluations on LongBench and SysBench demonstrate that LevelKV achieves state-of-the-art trade-offs between memory efficiency and instruction compliance. Remarkably, it maintains superior Instruction Hierarchy reliability even when retaining only 1/10 of the KV cache, enabling robust and efficient LLM deployment on memory-constrained devices.
author: Yizhen Yuan, Rui Kong, Bolin Xian, Yuanchun Li, Ting Cao, Xianyuan Zhan, Ya-Qin Zhang, Yunxin Liu

title: SpBatch: Reclaiming Lost Sparsity for Batched Sparse FFN Execution
content: Generative large language models (LLMs) face significant challenges in deployment due to their substantial computational and memory demands, particularly under batched inference scenarios. While activation sparsity offers a promising direction to reduce resource consumption, its benefits diminish with increasing batch sizes. Moreover, existing sparse inference systems fail to fully utilize modern GPU Tensor Cores. This paper proposes SpBatch, an efficient execution framework for batched activation-sparse FFN computation in ReLU-adapted LLMs through a two-level design. At the system level, it introduces Sparsity-Aware-Division to dynamically partition large batches into smaller mini-batches, maximizing sparsity and hardware utilization simultaneously. At the kernel level, it employs a “Load by CUDA Cores, Compute by Tensor Cores” strategy, alongside a Bitmap-based Neuron Index mechanism for load balancing and an optimized execution pipeline. SpBatch achieves up to 8.89${\boldsymbol{\times}}$× speedup over PowerInfer (a representative activation-sparse baseline) and up to 2.6${\boldsymbol{\times}}$× over llama.cpp (a dense inference framework) in end-to-end inference under the evaluated settings. These results demonstrate that activation sparsity and batch processing can be jointly leveraged through a selective sparse FFN execution path, especially in small-to-moderate batch regimes and high-sparsity edge-oriented scenarios where dense execution does not yet fully dominate.
author: Zhixiong Zhang, Zhongxiang Wei, Zhaohan Wang, Jin Zhao, Yuedong Xu, Xiaoming Fu

title: Beyond Reproducibility: Token Probabilities Expose Large Language Model Nondeterminism
content: The execution of Large Language Models (LLMs) on GPUs has been shown to exhibit nondeterministic behavior, even under deterministic settings, due to finite-precision arithmetic and the order of parallel operations. This poses challenges for deploying LLMs in dependable systems, because the lack of consistency represents a fundamental reliability issue that complicates for example the auditability and certification of LLM decision-making. Previous studies mainly focus on output variability or enforcing deterministic execution. To enable a deeper analysis, this work investigates the nondeterminism at the token probability level. Through extensive evaluations across multiple LLMs, GPU platforms, and configurations, consistent results in both the trends and quantitative variations of probabilities are observed: nondeterminism significantly affects token probabilities in the range of 0.1 to 0.9, while probabilities near 0 or 1 remain relatively stable. Based on the findings, significant implications and insights for understanding nondeterminism in LLMs are provided in this paper. i) Nondeterminism can meaningfully affect the generated text when the temperature is not zero by perturbing mid-range token probabilities; ii) its impact depends on model characteristics such as probability distributions and output length; iii) the effect of nondeterminism may potentially be estimated using a single inference by analyzing token-level probabilities, without requiring repeated runs. Finally, the data and code produced in this work is released publicly to facilitate further investigation.
author: Tairan Fu, Gonzalo Martínez, Javier Conde, Carlos Arriaga, Xiuyuan Qi, Shanshan Liu, Pedro Reviriego

title: Component-Based Reliability Assessment and Fault Diagnosis of Data Center Networks
content: With the rapid expansion of data center networks and the growing complexity of network topologies, network failures have become inevitable, rendering reliability evaluation critical for the stable operation of data center networks. However, the unique non-regular clique-based structure of the high-performance server-centric ECQDC network makes traditional reliability assessment and fault diagnosis methods inapplicable, and its $\boldsymbol{h}$h-component reliability and fault identification problems have not been studied yet. To tackle this issue, this paper proposes a Component-Based Fault Diagnosis Model (CFM) to evaluate the reliability of the ECQDC network. Firstly, we derive the exact expressions of $\boldsymbol{h}$h-component connectivity for ECQDC, which serves as the structural foundation of the proposed model. Secondly, we determine the $\boldsymbol{h}$h-component diagnosability of ECQDC based on the CFM, extending the relevant theory to non-regular network topologies. Thirdly, we develop the H-CDA algorithm to achieve efficient fault identification for large-scale ECQDC networks. Experimental results demonstrate that the CFM delivers excellent structural resilience, and the H-CDA algorithm achieves a diagnosis success rate of 99.1% under random fault scenarios while retaining 94.8% under correlated cluster faults, with an F1-score above 0.96 across all tested failure patterns. These achievements provide a solid theoretical and practical basis for the reliability optimization of the ECQDC network.
author: Xiangying Peng, Weibei Fan, Fu Xiao, Mengjie Lv, Xueli Sun, Wei Duan, Lei Han, Sun-Yuan Hsieh

title: RT-DPU: Scheduling Real-Time Tasks With Heterogeneous Multi-DPU Engines
content: The rapid growth of AI applications in real-time systems has heightened the demand for efficient acceleration techniques for convolutional neural network (CNN) inference. Field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) have emerged as a promising solution due to their energy efficiency and predictable timing behavior.
